title: ProjectConfig
description: The file a project writes — 'verifier.pact.yaml' on the provider side, 'consumer.pact.yaml' on the consumer side, the same document either way. It is a loader-side artifact: the loader interpolates its '${VAR}' references, reads the files it names and hands the engine a resolved HookConfig (ADR 0014). The difference between this schema and hook-config.schema.json is exactly the work the loader does, which is why the two are separate documents rather than one with optional members. See spec.md §6 and §7.

version.description: Configuration document version; 1 in this specification.

components.description: The components this project declares. Governed by design 2.6's ComponentConfig and deliberately not restated here — one member, one owner. Components and hooks share a file because they answer the same question ('what does this project load, and what may it do'), and splitting them would put a component's grants on a different page from the hook that needs them.

hooks.description: Lifecycle point -> the hooks declared at it, in the order they run.

AuthoredHook.title: AuthoredHook
AuthoredHook.description: A hook as written. Every string member may carry '${VAR}' references, which the loader replaces with environment values before the engine sees them; an unset variable fails the run at load, naming it, and never becomes an empty string (spec.md §7.2).

config.description: The hook's own configuration, before interpolation. This is where '${JANUS_SIGNING_SECRET}' is written — the secret's name lives in the repository, its value never does.

when.description: Selector; the When of hook-config.schema.json, unchanged by resolution.

changes.description: Dotted context paths this hook may replace.

AuthoredRun.title: AuthoredRun
AuthoredRun.description: As written: the same kinds as the resolved Run, plus the one member resolution removes — 'path', a script file the loader reads and inlines.

path.description: kind 'script': the script file, relative to the configuration file. The loader reads it, transpiles it when it is TypeScript (spec.md §9.6) and passes the result as 'source'; the engine never sees a path, because an engine that resolves paths is an engine whose runs depend on the directory it was started in.

source.description: kind 'script': the script inline, for a hook short enough to read in the configuration. Exactly one of 'path' and 'source' is present.

env.description: The environment the spawned child gets, in full — typically written as '${...}' references, which is how a credential reaches a state handler without being written down.
